partner_context.their_ambition: JIH Global set out to do what no one else had: re-platform the way an entire nation moves across water. Not a single resort transfer, not a pilot — a national foiling-electric network for the Maldives, capitalised and built as one program.
partner_context.their_pressure: A national mobility upgrade only works if it is bankable, deliverable and proven. Seaplanes and diesel speedboats are weather-bound, costly and carbon-heavy; the country needed a partner whose technology was real today and whose deployment could be financed and phased with confidence — not a science project.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier and JIH Global moved first. Together they signed a ~100-vessel, $100M, three-year program to deploy foiling-electric vessels across the Maldives — the largest deployment of foiling-electric vessels in tourism, structured, financed and already ramping. JIH Global is the vehicle that turned the thesis into a funded, executing national program.

hero.title: Navier × JIH Global — the proof that a national foiling network gets built
hero.subtitle: A ~100-vessel, $100M, three-year program to re-platform how the Maldives moves on water — signed, capitalised, and ramping now.
hero.what_we_do_together: JIH Global and Navier are deploying a foiling-electric vessel network at national scale across the Maldives. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path; JIH Global brings the program capital, the resort and atoll relationships, and the rollout sequence. This is not a memorandum or an intention — it is a structured, funded, phased program with the first vessels arriving in 2026. It is the reference deal every other archipelago and developer now points to when they ask whether marine mobility at scale is real.

why_now: The Navier × JIH Global agreement — ~100 vessels, $100M, a three-year phased rollout with the first 5 boats in 2026 — was reported by The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg in May 2026. It is the largest deployment of foiling-electric vessels in tourism, and it is already underway. For any partner weighing a marine-mobility program, JIH Global answers the only question that matters first: yes, a deal this size has been struck, financed and started.
multimodal_fit: JIH Global is the program layer that sits above the individual transfers: it aggregates demand across resorts, atolls and the capital region into one financed fleet program, so that any single resort or atoll can plug into a network rather than buy a boat. Navier provides the standardised platform; JIH Global provides the structure that lets the whole archipelago move as one system — airport to atoll hub to resort jetty.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: On-demand premium island-hopping between resorts, sandbanks and dive sites — the in-stay water layer.

JIH Global chose Navier because the fleet is real, standardised and improving over the air — bankable infrastructure, not a prototype.

proof_points.claim: The program is real, public and at scale.

objections.concern: Is a program this large actually deliverable?
objections.response: It is already being delivered — phased atoll-by-atoll under the signed agreement, with the first vessels arriving in 2026 and a three-year sequence behind them. The phasing de-risks delivery: each wave funds and proves the next.

objections.concern: Can the fleet handle open-atoll crossings and swell?
objections.response: The foil flies above the chop for a smoother ride than a diesel speedboat in the same conditions. Pioneer II covers intra- and near-atoll legs all-electric; the Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longest outer-atoll crossings with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: What about charging across remote islands?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at resort jetties; Quanta-LR needs no charging at all — the exact constraint that previously kept electric out of the outer atolls is removed by the platform mix.

objections.concern: Does this depend on replacing seaplanes overnight?
objections.response: No. Foiling takes the high-frequency near and mid-atoll legs (all-weather, after-dark, lower cost); seaplanes keep the longest, lowest-frequency routes. The program lifts reliability across the whole network rather than betting on a single switch.

phases.rationale: Launch where transfer volume is highest and the airport hub anchors the network; the first wave validates operations, training and the certification path.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance and certification path, and the operating playbook now being proven across the atolls.
the_ask.partner_brings: Program capital, resort and atoll relationships, the rollout sequence, local operating partnerships, and the national footprint that lets the fleet aggregate demand across the whole archipelago.
the_ask.next_step: Continue the phased deployment and publish the Maldives program as the global reference for how a national foiling network gets financed, built and operated.

close.title: The deal that proves it can be done.
close.body: JIH Global is the answer to the first question every developer, authority and operator asks: has anyone actually committed to marine mobility at scale? Yes — ~100 vessels, $100M, three years, ramping now. It is the precedent the rest of the world is now measured against.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. JIH Global is the first to act on it at national scale.

end_state.headline: A national foiling transfer layer, financed and built as one program.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every inhabited and resort atoll in the Maldives — ~26 natural atolls, 160+ resorts and the Greater Malé urban region — connected by a fast, silent, zero-emission foiling network capitalised under a single multi-year program.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II for inner/mid-atoll transfers; Quanta-LR for outer-atoll all-weather crossings
steady_state.tam_framing: ~2M annual visitors, nearly all requiring a transfer — re-platformed as one financed national network rather than hundreds of separate boat purchases.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the world's first archipelago-scale foiling network, capitalised and delivered as a single program: jet-to-foil-to-villa across the entire Maldivian atoll chain, the live reference case for how the planet's island-hopping markets get built.
